title: Rice Pilaf with Dried Fruit, Nuts and Spice

items.raw: 1 cinnamon stick, 4 green cardamom pods (lightly crushed), 3 whole cloves
½ teaspoon ground cumin, ¼ teaspoon ground turmeric
⅓ cup golden raisins or currants
⅓ cup sliced almonds and ¼ cup shelled pistachios
Chopped parsley or cilantro, to finish

steps.text: Rinse in a sieve under cold water, swirling, until the water runs mostly clear. Let it drain. Rinsing is what keeps the grains separate.
In a dry skillet over medium heat, toast the almonds and pistachios 3 to 4 minutes, stirring, until fragrant and lightly golden. Set aside.
Melt the butter in a heavy saucepan with a tight lid over medium heat. Cook the onion 8 to 10 minutes until soft and golden.
Add the cinnamon, cardamom, cloves, cumin, and turmeric and stir 1 minute until fragrant. Add the rice and stir 2 minutes to coat each grain in butter.
Add the stock, salt, apricots, and raisins and bring to a boil. Stir once, cover tightly, and turn the heat to the lowest setting. Cook 15 minutes without lifting the lid.
Take the pan off the heat and let it sit, still covered, 10 minutes. The rice finishes steaming in that time.
Fluff gently with a fork, fish out the whole spices, and fold in the toasted nuts and herbs.

notes.label: Don’t lift the lid
notes.text: every peek lets out steam the rice needs.

notes.label: Fruit choices
notes.text: dried cherries, cranberries, or chopped dates all work.

notes.label: Ahead of time
notes.text: reheat in a covered dish at 325°F with a splash of stock, adding the nuts only before serving so they stay crisp.

notes.label: Alongside
notes.text: roast lamb, chicken, or a holiday turkey.

openQuestion: Whose pilaf is this, and what does it go with — lamb, Thanksgiving, a holiday table? Which fruits and nuts does your version use?
